pages.text: Biology from the bottom up: the cell, its skin, its chemistry and its protein factory. Everything alive is made of these.

$(thing)Contamination$(): Biology machines do not explode, they catch things. Each run handles the culture and costs 4% sterility; below half, a run may bring something in, and the machine stops until it is cleaned. A $(item)Sterile Pack$() (from the $(item)Autoclave$()) always cleans it. An $(item)Antibiotic$() is cheaper, but each dose on the same machine selects for what survives it, so the n-th works only one time in n.

$(thing)Living cultures$(): yeast, algae and cells are alive. Carried loose or dropped they die off (half in a few days of carrying); machines and chests keep them. A dead culture is no use to any recipe.

$(thing)Membranes$(): the $(item)Patch-Clamp Rig$() sets the ions on each side of a membrane; the voltage, Nernst's E = (RT/zF) ln(c_out/c_in), must land in the recipe's window. Lipid Bilayers sit at potassium's −90 mV, Ion Channel Membranes at sodium's +60, and a $(item)Living Cell$() ($(thing)Respiration$()) at a resting −70.

$(thing)Fermentation$(): the $(item)Fermenter$() grows yeast with air and ferments without it; too much sugar holds it back. Yeast makes Nutrient Broth cheaply, and rotten flesh rots to biogas (methane). $(thing)Photosynthesis$(): the $(item)Photobioreactor$() grows algae that make oxygen and a far cheaper Quantum Chlorophyll; too bright and they bleach.

$(thing)Transcription$() and $(thing)Translation$(): the $(item)Ribosome Assembler$() reads messages. Faster is sloppier, and a chain is right only if every codon is. Messenger RNA makes Engineered Enzymes cheaply, and with a Living Cell, a Synthetic Cell. $(thing)Protein Folding$(): the $(item)Folding Chamber$() holds a chain below its melting point until 95% of it folds.
